answer: An NFL prediction market lets you buy and sell contracts on NFL outcomes (game winners, spreads, totals, props, division and Super Bowl futures) at prices in cents that equal the market's probability, with no bookmaker margin and the ability to sell before kickoff or at halftime. The main US venues are Kalshi, Polymarket US, Novig and ProphetX, all regulated by the CFTC. NFL contracts carry the deepest liquidity of any sport on these venues, and their prices routinely differ from sportsbook lines by one to three points.

sections.h2: How NFL prices compare with sportsbooks

blocks.p: On a standard spread a sportsbook charges -110 each side, a 4.76% overround. On a prediction market the same spread trades at, say, 50 cents bid, 51 offered, with a fee of a cent or two per contract. The round-trip cost is roughly 2% to 3% against 4.8%, and the break-even win rate falls from 52.4% to around 51%.

Prices also differ in direction. Sportsbooks shade popular favorites and overs because the public bets them; prediction markets have no house position and move on whoever trades last. The result is that public teams are often a point or two cheaper on the markets, and sharp sides a point or two cheaper at a sharp book. Watching both is how line shoppers find the gaps.

blocks.callout: Example from a 2026 Sunday: a road favorite at -3 was -112 at the two largest sportsbooks and 49 cents (about -104) on a prediction market an hour before kickoff. Same bet, 8 cents of price.

list: Lines open on Sunday night or Monday for the following week. Early markets are thin; spreads of three or four cents are common until Wednesday.
Depth builds Thursday through Saturday as injury reports land. By Sunday morning the main markets are tight.
The hour before kickoff is the deepest and the most volatile. Large orders move the price a cent or two and the gap to sportsbook lines opens and closes repeatedly.
Primetime games (Thursday, Sunday night, Monday) carry the most props and the deepest in-game trading.
Super Bowl futures trade all year, with the biggest volume in the two weeks before the game.

blocks.p: The feature NFL bettors notice first is the exit. A contract bought on a Tuesday at 44 cents that trades at 52 on Sunday after a favorable injury report can be sold for 8 cents of profit per contract without the game being played. Season-long futures work the same way: a Super Bowl contract bought at 6 cents in September and trading at 15 in December can be sold or partially sold, which is cheaper than hedging at a sportsbook's cash-out price.

The venues are CFTC-designated and operate nationwide, but sports contracts are the subject of an active fight between the venues and several states. Appeals courts have split, the CFTC is suing states, and petitions are pending at the Supreme Court as of November 2026. A few states have court orders restricting sports contracts for their residents; the venue hides those markets in affected states. Non-sports markets are unaffected.

takeaways: NFL contracts are the deepest sports markets on US prediction markets; Kalshi, Polymarket US, Novig and ProphetX are the main venues.
Round-trip cost is about half a sportsbook's -110 margin, and prices differ from books by one to three points in both directions.
Liquidity builds through the week and peaks in the hour before kickoff.
Contracts can be sold before or during the game, which replaces cash-out.

faq.q: Which prediction market is best for NFL?
faq.a: Kalshi has the deepest NFL order books across game lines, props and futures; Polymarket US is very deep on the biggest games and Super Bowl futures; Novig and ProphetX are sports-only and competitive on game lines. The best price moves between them.

faq.q: Can you bet NFL point spreads on a prediction market?
faq.a: Yes. Spread contracts trade as Yes/No on a team covering a stated number, priced in cents, with the total of both sides at about $1 rather than $1.05.

The venues are CFTC-regulated and operate nationwide. Sports contracts are contested by some states, and a few restrict them by court order as of November 2026. Each venue lists where its NFL markets are available.

faq.q: Can I sell an NFL contract before the game?
faq.a: Yes, at any time there is a buyer. That is how traders take profit after line moves or hedge season-long futures.

faq.q: Are NFL prices better on prediction markets than sportsbooks?
faq.a: Often by one to three points, because there is no margin in the price. Not always: a thin midweek market can have a wider spread than a book's -108 line. Compare before trading.

faq.q: Do prediction markets have NFL player props?
faq.a: On featured games, yes, with growing lists; outside primetime the props are thin or absent. Sportsbooks still have far more prop depth.
